thread:
incident-bot: Pager: multi-region failover detected — automatic traffic shift started from ap-southeast-2 -> us-east-1 and eu-west-1 at 1789456000, elevated 5xx spike and connection errors seen in ap-southeast-2. Severity: Sev2. @Tayla (oncall) paged. :rotating_light:
Tayla (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing 30% errors for /v1/gen from ap-southeast-2 region, latency up ~350ms. Any deploys?
Devon (infra): No deploys in the last 30m. Autoscaler is healthy. I see a regional egress error in our cloud provider console — a subset of AZs in ap-southeast-2 reporting network flap and intermittent BGP withdraws.
Maggie (sre): Confirming client-side logs show DNS timeouts then fallback to other regions — TTLs for frontend LB are 60s but we still see requests hang during switch.
Alex (neteng): Provider incident says "transit flapping in AZ b". Looks like a routing flap causing backend connections to drop; healthcheck failovers kicked in and traffic-shift policy moved sessions out.
Tayla (oncall): Can we pause automatic cross-region shifts while we investigate? We want to avoid oscillation.
Devon (infra): You can flip the routing policy to hold by setting policy.ctl.failover_enabled=false for the traffic-router service. Doing now:
```
# curl to control plane
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control.redwood.internal/traffic-router/policy -d '{"failover_enabled":false}'
```
OpsBot: control-plane: policy update accepted by traffic-router (req id 0a1b2c). failover_enabled=false
Alex (neteng): Good. That will stop further automatic shifts. We still need to drain sessions away from the unhealthy AZs that are already affected to avoid customer errors.
Maggie (sre): Start graceful drain for ap-southeast-2 AZ b instances, set max-in-flight to 10 and increase connection timeouts to avoid mid-request drops.
Devon (infra): Initiating drain: `infractl drain --region ap-southeast-2 --az b --timeout 900s --max-in-flight 10`
Tayla (oncall): Watching metrics — 50% drop in 5xx inside ap-southeast-2 within 2m of drain start, overall error rate across service down from 18% -> 4% but latency bumped in failover regions by ~60ms.
Jamal (product): Heads up to platform customers — which customers saw errors? Customer Success, can you pull impacted list?
Customer Success: Pulling. Preliminary: 8 customers with traffic concentrated in ap-southeast-2 saw elevated 5xx for ~8–12 minutes; none reported data loss, mostly transient request failures and timeouts. We'll prepare comms.
Alex (neteng): We see DNS TTL expirations causing some clients to retry old endpoints. Suggest reducing DNS TTL in ap frontend to 15s when we re-enable shifts so future flaps propagate faster.
Devon (infra): Noted. Also saw that our prefix advertisement to the transit provider timed out for ~80s due to a config churn in provider's route-reflector group — that's likely root cause. I'm opening ticket with provider, attaching BGP dump.
Maggie (sre): For now we should keep failover disabled until provider confirms stable — otherwise we'll oscillate. Also schedule a controlled manual traffic rebalancing later when stable.
Tayla (oncall): Agreed. Change summary: 1) disabled automatic failover at 1789456030 2) started AZ drain at 1789456052 3) monitored reduction in 5xx by 1789456140.
Devon (infra): Provider responded: "we applied fix to route reflector; sessions recovered at 1789456420". I validated BGP adjacencies restored.
Alex (neteng): Re-enabled routing failover but in manual canary mode: set failover_mode=canary and canary_fraction=0.05 to shift 5% of new sessions and observe.
Devon (infra): Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control.redwood.internal/traffic-router/policy -d '{"failover_mode":"canary","canary_fraction":0.05}'
```
OpsBot: control-plane: policy update accepted (req id 9f8e7d).
Tayla (oncall): Canary started at 1789456500. No spike in 5xx in first 3m. Increasing to 20% after 5m of stability.
Maggie (sre): Rolling the remainder back to normal routing completed by 1789456640. Postmortem action items: get eBGP session monitoring for route-reflector health, add faster DNS TTL fallback for frontend, and document manual failover playbook with exact control-plane commands.
Jamal (product): Customer comms draft: apologize for transient errors, note we mitigated by draining and rebalancing, give timeline, promise postmortem within 48h.
Customer Success: Will notify impacted customers with the draft. No escalations so far.
Tayla (oncall): Handoff to day-team: incident contained, automatic failover left in canary mode 20% for 10m then reverted to normal. I'll assign follow-ups to Devon/Alex/Maggie for postmortem. Oncall clear at 1789456720. :white_check_mark:
Maggie (sre): Adding monitoring alert refinement: add a composite alert that triggers only if cross-region 5xx spike AND provider BGP withdraws to avoid noisy paging.
Devon (infra): Filed provider ticket #INC-3421 and internal postmortem doc link: https://wiki.redwood/internal/incidents/1789456000 (will populate).
Tayla (oncall): Thanks team. Closing thread.
